idea.body: The Pythagorean theorem finds a right triangle's missing side: leg squared plus leg squared equals hypotenuse squared. A robot's ramp has legs 6 and 8 centimeters. Its hypotenuse is the square root of 36 plus 64, which is the square root of 100, or 10. Two special right triangles keep exact answers even when the square root is not whole. A 45-45-90 triangle's two legs are equal, and its hypotenuse is always a leg times the square root of 2. A 30-60-90 triangle's short leg, long leg and hypotenuse are always in the ratio 1 to the square root of 3 to 2. A short leg of 5 gives a long leg of 5 times the square root of 3, and a hypotenuse of 10.

figure.alt: A right triangle with legs 6 and 8 centimeters and hypotenuse 10.

workedExample.prompt: A drone's landing leg is a 45-45-90 triangle brace. Each of its two equal legs is 7 centimeters. What is the hypotenuse, in exact form?
steps: A 45-45-90 triangle's hypotenuse is always a leg times the square root of 2.
The leg is 7, so the hypotenuse is 7 times the square root of 2.
Written in exact form, that is 7 sqrt(2).

figure.alt: A 45-45-90 triangle with both legs 7 centimeters and the hypotenuse unknown.

ways.name: The formula
ways.when: Use this any time you know both legs of a right triangle.
steps: A ramp brace is a right triangle with legs 9 and 12 centimeters.
The Pythagorean theorem says leg squared plus leg squared equals hypotenuse squared.
Square each leg: 9 times 9 is 81, and 12 times 12 is 144.
Add them: 81 plus 144 is 225.
The hypotenuse is the square root of 225, which is 15 centimeters.
ways.example: A right triangle has legs 9 and 12 centimeters. Find the hypotenuse.
ways.trap: Adding the legs directly instead of squaring each one first.

figure.alt: A right triangle with legs 9 and 12 centimeters and an unknown hypotenuse.

frames.caption: leg squared + leg squared = hyp squared

ways.name: The triples
ways.when: Use this when the legs share a common factor with a known triple like 3-4-5.
steps: A camera mount is a right triangle with legs 15 and 20 centimeters.
Look for a common Pythagorean triple hiding in the legs, like 3-4-5.
Both legs share a factor of 5: 15 is 5 times 3, and 20 is 5 times 4.
The triangle is a 3-4-5 triple scaled by 5.
The hypotenuse is 5 times 5, which is 25 centimeters.
ways.example: A right triangle has legs 15 and 20 centimeters. Recognize the triple to find the hypotenuse.
ways.trap: Missing the shared scale factor and squaring and adding instead, which also works but invites more arithmetic slips.

figure.alt: A right triangle with legs 15 and 20 centimeters and an unknown hypotenuse.

frames.caption: Look for a 3-4-5 triple hiding here

ways.name: The special triangle templates
ways.when: Use this for a 45-45-90 or 30-60-90 triangle, to keep an exact answer with a root.
steps: A support brace is a 30-60-90 triangle with a short leg of 6 centimeters.
A 30-60-90 triangle's sides always follow the ratio 1 to square root of 3 to 2.
The short leg matches the 1 part of the ratio.
The long leg matches the square root of 3 part, so it is the short leg times square root of 3.
6 times square root of 3 is 6 sqrt(3) centimeters.
ways.example: A 30-60-90 triangle has a short leg of 6 centimeters. Find the long leg in exact form.
ways.trap: Multiplying the short leg by 2 to get the long leg instead of by the square root of 3.

figure.alt: A 30-60-90 triangle with the short leg 6 centimeters, the right angle marked, and an unknown long leg.

ways.name: The squares on the sides
ways.when: Use this to see the Pythagorean theorem as areas instead of a formula.
steps: A right triangle has legs 5 and 12 centimeters.
Draw a square on each leg.
The square on the 5 centimeter leg has area 5 times 5, which is 25.
The square on the 12 centimeter leg has area 12 times 12, which is 144.
The hypotenuse's square has area 25 plus 144, which is 169, so the hypotenuse is the square root of 169, or 13.
ways.example: A right triangle has legs 5 and 12 centimeters. Use squares on the legs to find the hypotenuse.
ways.trap: Adding the two leg lengths first instead of adding the two squared areas.

figure.alt: A right triangle with legs 5 and 12 centimeters, squares of area 25 and 144 built on the two legs.

frames.caption: Draw a square on each leg
